request:
Build a production-ready, visually stunning front-end web app for a fictional
company: "SILICON EXCHANGE" — a marketplace where people rent out idle GPUs and
AI accelerators by the hour. Renters browse listings, inspect utilization
charts, and reserve time blocks.

FRONT END ONLY. No backend, no database, no auth. All data is mock data defined
in code, but the app must behave like the real thing — the reservation logic,
the pricing math, and the filter state all have to actually work.

TECH STACK: Vite + React + TypeScript (strict). react-router-dom for routes.
Plain CSS with design tokens (no CSS framework). Charts are hand-rolled inline
SVG. React context + reducer for shared state. Vitest for unit tests. Zero paid
services and zero external network requests at runtime.

MOCK DATA (typed, deterministic, defined in src/data):
- 24 listings across at least 5 regions, with realistic chips (H100, RTX 5090,
  M3 Ultra, MI300X, RTX Pro 6000, etc.), memory in GB, TFLOPS, hourly rate in
  integer cents, and a status of "available" | "maintenance" | "retired".
- Hourly utilization samples per listing (0-100%), generated from a seeded
  pseudo-random function so charts look organic but render identically on every
  reload. Do NOT use Math.random() at render time.
- A handful of pre-existing reservations, including at least one that a naive
  overlap check would wrongly allow.

THE HARD PART — these rules must be pure, tested TypeScript functions:
1. Overlap detection. A listing cannot hold two reservations whose time ranges
   overlap. Ranges are half-open: a reservation ending at 14:00 and one starting
   at 14:00 do NOT overlap. Cancelled reservations don't count.
2. Pricing. Billed in 15-minute increments, always rounded UP. Minimum billable
   block is 1 hour. Any reservation longer than 24 continuous hours gets 10% off
   every hour beyond the 24th — not off the whole booking. All money is integer
   cents. Never use floating point for money.
3. Holds expire. A reservation held for more than 10 minutes without being
   confirmed flips to "expired" and frees its slot. Drive this off a real timer
   in the UI with a visible countdown.
4. Maintenance blocks new reservations but leaves existing confirmed ones alone.
5. Reservations persist to localStorage and survive a full page reload.

PAGES / ROUTES:
1) "/" Home — hero, a "GPUs online" counter computed from the real mock data,
   three feature cards, CTA into browse.
2) "/browse" — grid of listing cards with working search, region filter, memory
   range filter, status filter, and sort (price, memory, TFLOPS, utilization).
   Filter state lives in the URL query string and must survive a refresh AND the
   browser back button. Show an empty state when filters match nothing.
3) "/listings/:slug" — spec sheet, a 24-hour utilization line chart with a
   working hover tooltip, a 7-day availability calendar that visually blocks out
   taken slots, and a reservation form with a live price quote that recalculates
   as the user adjusts the time range. Show the pricing breakdown — base hours,
   rounding applied, discount applied.
4) "/dashboard" — the user's reservations from localStorage, with countdown
   timers on held ones, cancel buttons, and a running total spend.
5) "/compare" — pick up to 3 listings and diff their specs side by side.
   Selection persists across navigation.
6) A custom, on-brand not-found page (not the default).

DESIGN DIRECTION: Dark-first with a real light mode toggle that persists and
does not flash on reload. Technical-industrial: near-black surfaces, thin
hairline borders, monospace for all numbers and IDs, one electric accent color
used sparingly. Data-dense but calm — a trading terminal, not a SaaS template.
Hover lift on cards, visible focus states, smooth transitions. Responsive from
375px to 4K; tables collapse into cards on mobile; charts stay readable on a
phone. Accessibility: keyboard navigation, semantic headings, labelled form
controls, aria labels on icon buttons, and a text summary alternative for every
chart. No stock photography and no external image or font requests — every
visual is inline SVG or CSS; the app renders perfectly with the network off.

TESTS (must actually pass — npm test): Vitest unit tests covering at minimum
overlap detection including the half-open boundary case, the 15-minute
round-up, the 1-hour minimum, the over-24-hour discount applied only to the
excess hours, hold expiry at the 10-minute boundary, and the filter/sort logic
returning correct results for a combined query.

QUALITY BAR: Production-ready. No TODO comments, no stubbed functions, no any
types, no Lorem Ipsum, no dead buttons. Every control does something. npm
install, npm test, npm run build, npm run dev must all succeed.

planIncrements.title: App shell
planIncrements.objective: Render the SILICON EXCHANGE shell with nav, all six routes mounted empty, and a theme toggle, with no data or behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: App builds and opens showing nav and an empty home surface
All six routes render without error
Theme toggle is visible and clickable

planIncrements.title: Typed mock data
planIncrements.objective: Define 24 listings, seeded utilization samples, and pre-existing reservations as typed constants in src/data.
acceptanceCriteria: 24 listings span ≥5 regions with realistic chips, memory, TFLOPS, integer-cent rates, and status
Utilization samples are deterministic via seeded PRNG, no Math.random
At least one pre-existing reservation pair would pass a naive overlap check

planIncrements.title: Overlap detection
planIncrements.objective: Implement pure overlap detection with half-open ranges and cancelled-reservation exclusion.
acceptanceCriteria: A reservation ending at 14:00 and one starting at 14:00 do NOT overlap
Cancelled reservations are ignored in overlap checks
Vitest covers the boundary and cancelled cases

planIncrements.title: Pricing math
planIncrements.objective: Implement pure pricing: 15-min round-up, 1-hr minimum, 10% off hours beyond 24, all integer cents.
acceptanceCriteria: A 10-minute reservation bills as 1 hour
A 25-hour reservation applies 10% off only the 25th hour
Vitest covers round-up, minimum, and over-24h discount

planIncrements.title: Hold expiry
planIncrements.objective: Implement pure hold-expiry: a held reservation older than 10 minutes is expired and frees its slot.
acceptanceCriteria: A hold at exactly 10:00 is not expired; at 10:01 it is
Expired holds free their time slot
Vitest covers the 10-minute boundary

planIncrements.title: Maintenance blocking
planIncrements.objective: Implement pure rule: maintenance listings reject new reservations but retain confirmed ones.
acceptanceCriteria: A maintenance listing returns no available slots for new bookings
Existing confirmed reservations on a maintenance listing remain intact
Vitest covers both cases

planIncrements.title: Filter and sort logic
planIncrements.objective: Implement pure filter/sort: search, region, memory range, status, and sort by price, memory, TFLOPS, utilization.
acceptanceCriteria: A combined query (region + memory range + sort by TFLOPS) returns the correct ordered subset
Empty result set returned when no listing matches
Vitest covers a combined multi-criteria query

planIncrements.title: Shared state and persistence
planIncrements.objective: Wire React context + reducer for reservations and compare selection, persisted to localStorage.
acceptanceCriteria: A new reservation survives a full page reload
Compare selection persists across route navigation
Reducer handles add, confirm, cancel, and expire actions

planIncrements.title: Home page
planIncrements.objective: Render the home hero, live GPU-online counter from mock data, three feature cards, and a CTA to /browse.
acceptanceCriteria: GPU counter equals the count of available-status listings
CTA navigates to /browse
Three feature cards are visible

planIncrements.title: Browse page
planIncrements.objective: Render a filterable, sortable listing grid with URL-query-string state and an empty state.
acceptanceCriteria: Search, region, memory, status filters and sort all update the grid live
Filter state survives refresh and browser back button
Empty state message shows when no listings match

planIncrements.title: Spec sheet and utilization chart
planIncrements.objective: Render the spec sheet and a 24-hour inline-SVG utilization line chart with hover tooltip.
acceptanceCriteria: Spec sheet shows chip, memory, TFLOPS, rate, and status
Hovering the chart shows a tooltip with hour and percentage
A text summary alternative for the chart is present

planIncrements.title: Availability calendar
planIncrements.objective: Render a 7-day calendar that visually blocks out taken and held time slots.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirmed-reservation slots appear blocked
Held slots appear in a distinct state
Maintenance listings show all slots blocked for new bookings

planIncrements.title: Reservation form with live pricing
planIncrements.objective: Add a reservation form with time-range picker and a live quote showing base hours, rounding, and discount.
acceptanceCriteria: Adjusting the time range recalculates the quote in real time
Breakdown shows base hours, rounding applied, and discount applied
Submitting creates a held reservation visible in the calendar

planIncrements.title: Dashboard
planIncrements.objective: Show the user's reservations with countdown timers on held ones, cancel buttons, and running total spend.
acceptanceCriteria: Held reservations display a live countdown to expiry
Cancelling a reservation removes it and frees its slot
Total spend sums all confirmed reservations in integer cents

planIncrements.title: Compare page
planIncrements.objective: Allow selecting up to 3 listings and diff their specs side by side.
acceptanceCriteria: Selecting a 4th listing is blocked
Specs render in aligned columns for up to 3 listings
Selection persists when navigating away and back

planIncrements.title: Not-found page
planIncrements.objective: Render a custom on-brand 404 page for unmatched routes.
acceptanceCriteria: Navigating to an unknown path shows the custom 404
The 404 page includes a link back to home

planIncrements.title: Polish
planIncrements.objective: Apply the dark-first industrial theme, light-mode toggle, responsive layout, accessibility, and transitions across all routes.
acceptanceCriteria: Dark and light themes render with no flash on reload; toggle persists
Layout is responsive 375 px to 4K; tables collapse to cards on mobile
All controls have visible focus states, aria labels, and keyboard navigation works
All numeric values (prices, TFLOPS, memory, utilization percentages) and listing identifiers/slug IDs render in a monospace font family, distinguishable from the body sans-serif.
With DevTools network set to Offline, every page renders all visuals (charts, icons, backgrounds) correctly with zero failed network requests in the console.
